newsitem.title: UK: Brazil govt, industry differ over ethanol - Czarnikow.
newsitem.headline: Brazil govt, industry differ over ethanol - Czarnikow.

text.p: Differing views of industry and government in Brazil over the ethanol sector may lead to important readjustments as the national crop plan nears completion, Czarnikow Sugar said on Thursday.
In its monthly report, Czarnikow said Sao Paulo producers had forecast a rise of almost nine percent in cane output in their state for next season to 185.5 million tonnes.
This indicated an increase of 0.4 billion litres in alcohol to 9.4 billion in the coming season but a 20 percent rise in sugar to 9.63 million tonnes tel quel.
But the government view was that an increase of between one and two billion litres from cane would be needed in 1997/98 to replace fuel alcohol imports.

"This distribution of anticipated cane supplies may well reflect the industry's uncertainty over the proposed deregulation of anhydrous ethanol which is scheduled to be launched next month," Czarnikow said.

"In practice this is a major step and it is quite possible that a deferment will take place but there is nevertheless a strong likelihood that, at some stage over the coming season, the anhydrous ethanol sector may face important readjustments."

Sao Paulo producers account for almost 74 percent of all Brazil's centre-south cane. Czarnikow added that the producers' figures indicated industry expectations of a gradual switch from hydrous towards anhydrous ethanol.
There was clearly a gap between the government's plans for the coming season and the more commercial judgement of the industry, the report said.
"No doubt the two will come together as the crop plan is brought to a conclusion," it said.
The Brazilian government has said it wants to source all 1997/98 alcohol requirements from domestic cane production.
